relevance.rationale: Identity confirmed from the document's own cover (arXiv:2410.20973v1 [math.GT], summability for state integrals of hyperbolic knots, two authors) and matches the seeded key. Two citation sites, both load-bearing, both locators VERIFIED. (1) QOU/Mathlib/BorelStateIntegralSummability.lean:5,59,72 is declared 'Conditional on [fantini-wheeler2024], arXiv:2410.20973 Thm 1.4' and axiomatised as a Lean class. Theorem 1.4 EXISTS and reads: the asymptotic series Phi_Xi(-2 pi i / tau) are Borel-Laplace summable with Stokes rays on a countable set of rays with two accumulation points at arg(tau) = +- pi/2. The corpus's use is faithful, and carrying it as a named conditional class rather than as a proved lemma is the correct §3b-cond disposition. (2) QOU/QBeta/StateIntegralRecursionLattice.lean:60 cites 'eq. (14)'. Equation (14) EXISTS and is a recursion on the state integrals I_{m,l}: sum_k binom(B,k)(-1)^k q^{-l k} I_{m+k,l} = I_{m,l+1} = (-1)^A q^{A+m} I_{m+A,l}. The document uses it exactly as a lattice relation (e.g. at eqs. (66) and (67), 'where the equality follows from Equation (14)'), which matches the citing file's name and purpose. Also verified: the abstract states the document PROVES the Garoufalidis-Gu-Marino conjectures for 4_1 and 5_2 and gives an algorithm computing the Borel-Laplace resummation as a combination of Andersen-Kashaev state integrals, allowing explicit Stokes-constant computation — consistent with the ref() note.

keyResults.statement: The asymptotic series Phi_Xi(-2 pi i / tau) are Borel-Laplace summable, with Stokes rays lying on a countable set of rays having two accumulation points at arg(tau) = +- pi/2.
keyResults.useForFolio: It is the sole hypothesis of the BorelStateIntegralSummability conditional class; the class is honest precisely because this is an external theorem the folio does not prove.

keyResults.statement: A finite-difference recursion among the state integrals I_{m,l}: a binomial-weighted alternating sum in m equals I_{m,l+1} equals a q-power multiple of I_{m+A,l}.
keyResults.useForFolio: It is the lattice relation StateIntegralRecursionLattice.lean formalises, and the document applies it concretely in its 4_1 worked example, so the folio's use is on the same objects the source computes with.
